story: The Cascade Colonels, an Oregon string band with bassist Chad Kimbler, played Pickathon in 2004.
Cross-Eyed Rosie, a progressive acoustic band from Portland, played Pickathon in 2004 and again in 2008.

intro: A banjo player with a shifting cast of bandmates.
story: Danny Barnes brought one of his shape-shifting ensembles to Pickathon in 2004, a year after Dirt on the Angel, the first of two records for Terminus. A live album, Livin' Large, followed on Terminus that year.

The Freak Mountain Ramblers, Portland's psych-country band, had held a Sunday happy hour at the Laurelthirst since the fall of 1997, a show known as Church. They played Pickathon in 2004, and the Oregon Music Hall of Fame inducted them on October 13, 2018.

Hillstomp, the Portland duo of Henry Kammerer and John Johnson, met in 2001 and built a hill country blues stomp from guitar, banjo and a kit of buckets. They played Pickathon in 2004. Willamette Week named The Woman That Ended the World its 2005 Album of the Year, and the band later landed in the third season of Sons of Anarchy.
Jo Miller & Her Burly Roughnecks, a Northwest country and Western swing band, played Pickathon in 2004.

intro: A Dublin-born button accordion player living in Portland.
story: Johnny B. Connolly, a Dublin-born button accordion player, joined the Celtic band Anam at 17 and moved to Portland in 1997. He signed with Green Linnet in 2001 on the strength of a friendship with fiddler Kevin Burke, and played Pickathon in 2004. He later toured as a member of the Irish band Solas.
The Leah Larson Band, a Pacific Northwest acoustic act, played Pickathon in 2004.

Mark Lemhouse, a Portland guitarist who mixes blues, old country and folk, played Pickathon in 2004. His album The Great American Yard Sale won the Cascade Blues Association's Muddy Award for national recording in 2013. He plays with harmonica player David Lipkind and a band, the Woodbrains.

Po' Girl, the Vancouver roots band of Allison Russell and Trish Klein, played Pickathon in 2004, the year of Vagabond Lullabies and a year after its self-titled debut. The band made seven recordings, ending with Follow Your Bliss in 2010.
Spigot, an indie rock band, played Pickathon in 2002 and again in 2004.

The Government Issue Orchestra, a Portland old-time band with punk roots, was playing a punk-house kitchen in 2001 so hard the crowd's stomping bowed the floor. Bill Martin, a member, was also a square dance caller, and the band played Pickathon's square dance in 2004.
The Kenton County Regulators, a regional string band, played Pickathon in 2004.
The Shiftless Rounders, an old-time string band, played Pickathon in 2004 and again in 2005.

The Tallboys, a Seattle old-time string band, played Pickathon in 2004 and again in 2007. They hosted a twice-monthly Monday square dance at the Tractor Tavern that drew more than 100 people, and Fresh Daily came out in 2013.
